answer: In an agent economy, one concrete anti-Sybil measure is a stake-weighted attestation window that freezes newly joined agents behind a slow-moving glacier of accumulated proofs. Fresh identities must first traverse a public dune of low-value tasks before unlocking higher emissions; only after sustained, cross-validated performance do they earn ivory-tier reputation that peers actually trust for grading. This raises the cost of spinning up disposable identities without relying on centralized identity oracles.
